name: Pregabalin + Nortriptyline
meta: Pregabalin: Gabapentinoid (neuropathic pain / anxiolytic / antiepileptic); Nortriptyline Hydrochloride: Tricyclic antidepressant (secondary amine)
Pregabalin: N02BF02 (previously N03AX16); Nortriptyline Hydrochloride: N06AA10
Prescription-only fixed-dose combination. Components – Pregabalin: Schedule H –
prescription only; Nortriptyline Hydrochloride: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: White to off-white crystalline solid, freely soluble in water.
White to off-white powder (hydrochloride), soluble in water.

Pregabalin: Developed as a more potent successor to gabapentin; pain relief may begin within the first week. First approval/introduction: Synthesised 1990 (Richard B. Silverman, Northwestern University); EU and US FDA 2004 (Pfizer).
Nortriptyline Hydrochloride: The N-desmethyl active metabolite of amitriptyline; first described and patented in 1962. First approval/introduction: Introduced 1963; US approval 1964 (Geigy).
Combines alpha-2-delta ligand activity with noradrenergic descending pain inhibition; nortriptyline also improves sleep. Allows effective analgesia at lower individual doses.

Pregabalin Binds the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels with higher affinity than gabapentin, decreasing release of excitatory neurotransmitters; analgesic, anxiolytic and anticonvulsant. Receptor / target profile: Binds the alpha-2-delta-1 protein of voltage-gated calcium channels with high affinity, reducing release of glutamate, norepinephrine and substance P.

Nortriptyline Hydrochloride Predominantly inhibits norepinephrine reuptake (and serotonin to a lesser extent); enhances descending noradrenergic pain inhibition. Fewer anticholinergic and sedative effects than amitriptyline. Receptor / target profile: Potent NET inhibitor (Ki 1.8–4.4 nM) and moderate SERT inhibitor (Ki 15–18 nM); weaker H1 and muscarinic antagonism than amitriptyline.
Summary: Bioavailability ≥90% (linear); Tmax ~1 h. Not protein bound; negligible metabolism. Half-life ~6.3 h. Renally excreted unchanged – adjust dose to CrCl.
Summary: Well absorbed; Tmax 7–8.5 h. ~92% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP2D6. Half-life 18–44 h.
Peripheral neuropathic pain – diabetic neuropathy, post-herpetic neuralgia
One tablet once daily at bedtime; may increase to twice daily
Elderly – start low; monitor sedation and anticholinergic effects
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
CrCl ≥60: 150–600 mg/day; 30–60: 75–300; 15–30: 25–150; <15: 25–75 mg/day; supplement after dialysis.
Preferred TCA in elderly (less anticholinergic); still start low.
Small amounts in milk; use with caution.
Recent myocardial infarction, arrhythmias, heart block
Peripheral oedema – caution in heart failure
Pregabalin: With or without food; avoid alcohol.
Pregabalin: Renal function; weight; oedema; misuse; respiratory status.
Nortriptyline Hydrochloride: Plasma levels (therapeutic window 50–150 ng/mL for depression); ECG in cardiac disease.

Pregabalin: Somnolence, confusion, agitation, restlessness, seizures (rare), coma. Supportive care; haemodialysis effective. Nortriptyline Hydrochloride: As for TCAs – arrhythmias, seizures, coma. ECG monitoring and supportive care.
Supported by combination principle shown by Gilron et al. (Lancet 2009) with gabapentinoid + TCA; no large trials of this fixed combination.
Dizziness, drowsiness and weight gain may occur
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
